question: At fixed Eevee T08 and scene-linear EXR32, does strict variation recur between repeated renders of the same frame inside one initialized Blender process, or only across process initialization?

design.type: same-frame repeated-render versus fresh-process boundary with three process replicates

exactGate.withinPersistent: All 108 same-process repeated-render comparisons must be exact.
exactGate.persistentCrossProcess: All 108 same-ordinal cross-process comparisons must be exact.
exactGate.freshCrossProcess: All 36 fresh-process comparisons must be exact.

decisionRule.PROCESS_INITIALIZATION_BOUNDARY_SUPPORT: Within-PERSIST is exact 108/108 while both PERSIST cross-process and FRESH cross-process gates are non-exact, with a valid experiment.
decisionRule.PER_RENDER_VARIATION_SUPPORT: Within-PERSIST is non-exact, with a valid experiment, regardless of the two cross-process gates.
decisionRule.VARIATION_NOT_REPRODUCED: All three gates are exact, with a valid experiment.
decisionRule.MIXED_CROSS_PROCESS_PATTERN: Within-PERSIST is exact but the PERSIST and FRESH cross-process exactness gates disagree, with a valid experiment.
decisionRule.INVALID_EXPERIMENT: Any identity, source-state, intervention, process, call-count, EXR layout, image, binding, count or attack gate fails.

requiredNegativeCases: PERSIST render count differs from three
FRESH render count differs from one
render ordinals or same-frame invariant mismatch
process IDs are not unique across the 72 planned processes
cross-process comparison loses both manifest/file bindings
explicitNonClaims: A stable same-process result would support an initialization boundary under this profile but would not identify a driver, shader-cache, allocator or source-level mechanism.
A non-exact same-process result would locate recurrence at each render invocation or later; it would not by itself prove a race.
Three repeated renders and three process replicates falsify strict determinism but do not estimate mismatch probability.
The PERSIST cell intentionally holds the frame constant and therefore does not measure prior-frame temporal history.
No perceptual tolerance is selected and near-equality remains non-exact.
Nothing generalizes to Cycles, another GPU/backend, another machine or another scene.
